subject: maths

moments.title: Hardy-Littlewood collaboration
moments.who: G. H. Hardy, J. E. Littlewood, Cambridge
moments.body: Hardy and Littlewood collaborate from 1911 to 1947 — perhaps the most productive partnership in mathematical history. They wrote nearly 100 joint papers covering analytic number theory.

moments.title: Ramanujan in Cambridge
moments.body: Hardy brings the self-taught Ramanujan from Madras to Cambridge. Ramanujan's intuitive results are validated by Hardy's rigorous techniques. Ramanujan dies in 1920 at 32.
moments.takeaway: A rigorous Cambridge mathematician midwives a self-taught Indian genius.

moments.title: A Mathematician's Apology
moments.body: Hardy's elegant memoir defends pure mathematics. Famous lines: 'A mathematician, like a painter or a poet, is a maker of patterns.' He boasts his work has no practical use — number theory cannot be applied to war.
moments.takeaway: A defence of pure mathematics — about to be overtaken by events.

moments.title: Number theory in cryptography
moments.body: Hardy's beloved number theory now secures every credit card transaction on Earth. His prized purity has become foundational to global commerce.
moments.takeaway: Pure mathematics becomes essential applied mathematics.

now.title: Where we are today
now.body: Hardy-Littlewood circle method, prime distributions, and analytic techniques remain foundational. Hardy's Apology is still in print.
now.open_questions: What other 'pure' mathematics will become essential applied mathematics?

reflection: Hardy boasted his work was useless. It now secures the internet. Can mathematics ever be safely 'pure'?
